# SA tribunal lifts minimum standard 6% to $1,023 a week, declining to adopt the $1,004.90 national figure

The South Australian Minimum Standard for Remuneration rises 6% to $1,023.00 a week from the first full pay period on or after 1 July 2026. The Employment Tribunal declined to simply adopt the national minimum wage dollar figure of $1,004.90, which would have delivered a 4.12% increase in South Australia.

Published 26 September 2026

4 min read

South Australian Employment Tribunal

The wage floor for South Australian state awards will be $1,023.00 a week from the first full pay period on or after 1 July 2026, after the South Australian Employment Tribunal applied a 6% increase to the Minimum Standard for Remuneration rather than adopting the national minimum wage figure of $1,004.90 per week, or $26.44 an hour.

The decision, _State Wage Case 2026 (No 2)_ \[2026\] SAET 121, was delivered on 21 September 2026 by President Justice Dolphin, Commissioner Watkins and Commissioner Smith, and was heard and determined on the papers.

Under [s 100A](https://onnotice.com.au/news/section/s-100a/) of the _Fair Work Act 1994_ (SA), the Tribunal can take up the outcomes of the Fair Work Commission’s Annual Wage Review without hearing evidence or submissions, so long as no interested party objects. Because objections were lodged, the matter proceeded de novo, that is, afresh. A notice appeared in _The Advertiser_ and on the Tribunal’s website on 22 June 2026, proposing that the Minimum Standard for Remuneration be lifted to the national figures.

The two standards do not align. In 2025 the national minimum wage was $948.00 a week and the South Australian standard was $965.10. The Annual Wage Review 2026 lifted the national minimum wage to $1,004.90, a 6% increase, while setting 4.75% for modern award minimum rates. Applying the $1,004.90 dollar figure to the higher state standard would have produced an increase of 4.12%.

All interested parties submitted

that the Tribunal should take the analytical approach and increase the Minimum Standard for Remuneration by 6%, being the percentage movement in the national minimum wage. The interested parties were SA Unions, the Minister for Industrial Relations and Public Sector, the Chief Executive of the Attorney General’s Department, the Local Government Association of South Australia, the Corporation of the City of Adelaide and the United Firefighters’ Union of South Australia. None supported a 4.12% increase to $1,004.90, and none supported a 4.75% increase.

The United Firefighters’ Union submitted

that the terms of the 22 June notice constituted jurisdictional error, that the notice was void, and that it should be reissued showing the 6% increase.

The Full Bench found

that the analytical approach should be taken, holding: “The correct outcome of the Annual Wage Review is that the NMW was adjusted from $948.00 to $1,004.90, which is a 6% increase”. On the notice, it held the union’s submissions were “misconceived”, because the notice complied with s 100A(4)(b)(i) and (ii), and because the remedy for disagreement with a proposed declaration is an objection and the de novo hearing that follows.

The Bench also rejected alignment with the national figure as a reason to adopt it.

“There is history of the NMW and the MSR not aligning, with the latter being the greater, and no submissions have been received to argue that there should now be an alignment.” State Wage Case 2026 (No 2) \[2026\] SAET 121

On the meaning of “outcomes” in s 100A(3), the Bench held the word is shorthand for the breadth of the empowering provision in [s 100](https://onnotice.com.au/news/section/s-100/)(1).

Fair Work Act 1994 (SA), s 100(1)

> “in whole or in part, and with or without modification, principles, guidelines, conditions, practices or procedures”

The declaration sets an hourly rate of $26.92 for weekly hired adult employees working less than 38 hours a week, and for hours worked beyond ordinary hours, with $33.65 an hour for adult casuals. Junior rates are graded from 50% of the adult rate for those under 17 years of age to 90% at 20 years of age. The minimum amount payable under the supported wage provisions rises to $117.44 per week.

The earlier judgment of 7 September 2026, _State Wage Case 2026_ \[2026\] SAET 115, lifted minimum award rates, together with minimum work-related allowances and loadings in state awards, by 4.75%. Where a rate so increased falls below $1,023.00 per week, it is varied to that amount.

#### At a glance

- **Parties:** Interested parties included SA Unions, the Minister for Industrial Relations and Public Sector, the Chief Executive of the Attorney General’s Department, the Local Government Association of South Australia, the Corporation of the City of Adelaide and the United Firefighters’ Union of South Australia
- **Citation:** State Wage Case 2026 (No 2) \[2026\] SAET 121
- **Sections:** [ss 69](https://onnotice.com.au/news/section/s-69/), 100 and 100A, Fair Work Act 1994 (SA)
- **Outcome:** Minimum Standard for Remuneration increased by 6% to $1,023.00 per week
- **Who it affects:** Employers and employees covered by the awards listed in Schedule A, plus all employers and employees subject to the Act for the purposes of the minimum standard

The declaration applies to the awards in Schedule A, which include the Police Officers Award (PS), the Nurses (South Australian Public Sector) Award 2002 (PS), the Teachers Award (PS), the SA Ambulance Service Award (PS) and the Local Government Employees Award (LG). A party to an award may apply within 28 days after the making of the standard, under [s 72A](https://onnotice.com.au/news/section/s-72a/)(5), to have the award excluded from the standard or part of it. Each award will also carry a term allowing an employer or group of employers to apply to reduce, postpone or phase in the increase on the grounds of serious economic adversity, with the President to decide whether such an application is dealt with by a Full Bench.

Source: [\[2026\] SAET 121](https://www.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/cases/sa/SAET/2026/121.html)
